param_sources.w: Fecundability 0.15-0.25/month in natural-fertility populations; Wood 1994 (Dynamics of Human Reproduction), Hutterite fecundability by age and parity (Demography 1993).
param_sources.i: Bongaarts 1978 proximate-determinants framework; postpartum infecundability is the dominant interval component under prolonged breastfeeding. Cross-refs A.13.
param_sources.g_L: Gestational distribution of recognised loss: Wilcox et al. 1988 (NEJM), Macklon et al. 2002 (Hum Reprod Update), 'Biological Causes of Foetal Loss' (1993).
param_sources.r: Time added per loss, Bongaarts and Potter 1983; recovery interval after early loss, Schisterman et al. 2016 (Obstet Gynecol, trying to conceive after an early loss).
param_sources.T: Exposed span within marriage under the European and non-European marriage patterns; cross-refs A.7.

scenario_sources.PM_high_morbidity: Upper end anchored on populations with endemic malaria, syphilis and undernutrition; WFS-era estimates across eight countries (Social Biology 1989) and the Varanasi pregnancy-wastage cohort. Under-reporting means recorded rates are floors, so the range is drawn wide.
scenario_sources.PM_low_morbidity: Recognised-loss rates in low-morbidity natural-fertility populations; Hutterite prospective series.
scenario_sources.FDT_start_c1870: Late-fetal death alone ran 40-50 per 1000 births in nineteenth-century Europe (Woods 2009); early loss is unobserved and is inferred from contemporary recognised-loss rates plus a morbidity premium.
scenario_sources.FDT_end_c1965: Stillbirth rates fell to roughly 10-15 per 1000 by the 1960s in northern Europe (Danish post-1940 decline, Population Studies 2010); early-loss component assumed near contemporary levels.
scenario_sources.contemporary: Blencowe et al. 2016 stillbirth estimates; Quenby et al. 2021 miscarriage prevalence; NSFG self-reported loss trend 1990-2011.

target_binding_regime.note: Where a parity target binds and the span does not, the couple replaces the loss and completed fertility is unchanged. The model returns the target by construction, which is the point: B.5's effect is a property of the fertility regime, not of the loss rate alone.
